expectations.evidence: Section 1's main argument is about reach and effort. Push reaches only people who installed the app and allowed notifications, while the email list reaches every registrant. Even at 80% installs, 100 people still need email, so the team would staff two channels and send every message twice. The schedule is locked, so live updates are rarely needed, and promoting the app depends on the email list anyway. expectations.text: Grounds the recommendation in reach and effort rather than in the $4,800 price.
expectations.evidence: Most of the 'Why' section argues from reach. It treats the 80% claim as a poor fit, estimates a 15–30% install rate (75–150 people), notes that push only reaches installers who opt in while email reaches every registrant, and says the push feature solves a problem the event doesn't have. Effort comes up only lightly: attendees would have to download the app on venue wifi, and the static page takes 'an afternoon'.
